newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Ericsson says air cargo full to Far East.
newsitem.headline: Ericsson says air cargo full to Far East.

text.p: Swedish telecoms group LM Ericsson's mobile telecoms unit said on Tuesday it was having difficulty finding air cargo capacity to the Far East and within Europe from Sweden.
"We have a problem, with many destinations, to find space -- like Taipei, Jakarta and to other destinations as well as in Europe," Ericsson Radio shipping manager Thomas Hancock said.
Ericsson Radio is the largest shipper of goods by air freight in Sweden. Ericsson Radio often has to arrange charter flights in order to secure the capacity it needs, Hancock said.
"We want to move 35 cubic metres overnight to Athens and we can't do it without making special arrangements," Hancock said.
"Today we have a 747 chartered to Taipei with 85 tonnes. Next week we have another 85 tonnes so it can't wait," he said.
Ericsson Radio arranged about six charters so far this year to China, which is still a key destination for Ericsson mobile telephones, Hancock said.
"China is still very important. We are working in 11 or 12 provinces so it's not a single city that is especially important," he said.
"We are using all possible carriers -- SAS to Beijing, KLM, Air France especially to Shanghai...and Lufthansa and Finnair," Hancock said.
Hancock said he was seeing steady development.
"This is nothing spectacular compared to previous years. We don't foresee any changes at all. It's going along in a predictable fashion," he said.
